The Deputy President of the Senate, Barau I. Jibrin, has applauded the Nigerian Army for the deployment of a new battalion and an artillery regiment to Kano State, describing it as a strategic and timely intervention to strengthen security in the state and the North-West geopolitical zone.
Senator Barau, who commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf, said the establishment of the 24 Battalion in Tudun Wada and the 311 Artillery Regiment in Dambatta was a clear demonstration of the president’s unwavering commitment and resolve to combat all forms of violent criminality across the country. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the Deputy President of the Senate also commended the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant-General Waidi Shaibu for his “visionary leadership and proactive steps” in repositioning the Nigerian Army to confront security challenges.
“This strategic deployment is highly commendable. It underscores the commitment of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, to decisively deal with insecurity and secure the lives and properties of all Nigerians”, the statement added.
He also lauded the governor of Kano State, Abba Kabir Yusuf, an engineer, for his dedication and commitment to the security of lives and property in the state, noting that the synergy between the state government and the military is critical to achieving full operational capability of the new units.
Senator Barau further appealed to the host communities in Dambatta, Tudun Wada and the entire Kano State to always avail their unflinching support to the Nigerian Army and other security agencies.
“The fight against banditry and other forms of criminality is a collective one. I urge all our traditional leaders, community leaders and residents to cooperate fully with the military, share timely intelligence and support these newly established formations to succeed. Without community support, our security agencies cannot fully defeat these criminals,” he said.
He reaffirmed that the Senate would continue to provide the necessary legislative support and ensure adequate resources for the armed forces and other security agencies to defeat banditry and all forms of crime in the country.
